integrity: The proof reduces the published two-facet volume expression to endpoint optimization in one scalar variable. The nontrivial endpoint becomes a two-by-two Rayleigh quotient whose top eigenvalue gives the closed form. A separate feasibility argument constructs an inward normal realizing the lower endpoint and proves that exactly two facets are upper. A standalone checker replays the algebra and feasibility numerically over many dimensions; finite checks are not used as an infinite proof.
scientific_limitations: The result optimizes only the chamber in which exactly two facets are upper. For dimensions n>=6 it supplies a rigorous lower benchmark for the global problem but does not prove that two upper facets are globally optimal. The published prism-volume identity and upper-facet inequalities are used as premises. Unindexed or differently phrased prior work remains a residual originality risk.
title: Exact two-upper-facet benchmark for reflected regular simplices
